thread:
chloe_support: Heads up — customer AtlasHealth reporting large tail latency spikes on their Dedicated pool after we moved them to a 1+3 MIG partition layout this morning. 99th pct jumps from ~180ms to 1.2s under light qps (~5 rps). They see occasional API 429s too.

sam_eng: Thanks, Chloe. Do we have request traces or sample request IDs from the customer? 429s imply throttling on our side or local client-side retries.

matt_customer: @chloe_support attaching a short timeline and a few request IDs in the support ticket: RH-9241. Spikes started ~08:30 UTC after we reprovisioned the pool to 1g. We saw bursts when many short chat completions came in concurrently.

chloe_support: Copying their sanitized snippet: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","prompt":"x","max_tokens":64}'` returning 429 / some 200s that take >1s. Also pasted `nvidia-smi dmon` snapshot and MIG config from the node.

hemant_infra: Paste the `nvidia-smi` snippet here? curious whether SM utilization or memory bandwidth is pegged. MIG can still have cross-slice interference if slices share L3 or NVLink resources.

matt_customer: Here are the bits: ```
Timestamp Util% GPUm %
08:44 96  28
08:45 70  30
...```
And MIG config: `1g.10gb + 3g.20gb` on a single A100 node.

tess_sre: Noting the autoscaler bumped them from 1->2 nodes briefly around 09:10, then scaled back. Autoscale bot shows `scale-up` but a lagged warmup; could be cold-start thrash. @autoscale-bot can you dump the event log?

autoscale-bot: Event log: `08:30 scale-policy-eval: desired=2, provision_time_est=45s; 09:12 scale-up: added node-az2-14; 09:22 scale-down: removed node-az2-14`. Warmup time for model rwd-medium ~22s for kernel JIT and KV cache populating.

sam_eng: Two hypotheses: 1) SM saturation / memory bandwidth on the host when many small requests hit different MIG slices causing cache/TLB pressure; 2) Our serving runtime is serializing KV cache updates across slices -> queuing. We need perf counters and runtime debug logs for the timeframe. @hemant_infra can we enable `PERF_RAW` capture on a repro node?

hemant_infra: I spun up a reproducible test harness that mimics their request pattern (5 rps of short completions with concurrency=6). Repro shows 95th-99th jump when concurrency spikes to 12. Collected `nvprof` style counters: SM active cycles high, L2 read/write latency increased, `nvlink` not saturated. Looks like L2/L3 contention.

sam_eng: Good find. That aligns with cross-slice L2 thrash. Mitigations: 1) Temporarily move AtlasHealth to an isolated MIG node (no other tenants) to confirm noisy neighbor is the issue; 2) Increase dedicated pool throttle config to smooth concurrency (token-bucket) while we investigate; 3) For long-term, recommend different MIG partitioning (e.g., 2x2g instead of 1+3) or full-card for critical customers.

matt_customer: Can you do the isolation test now? Their SLA requires <300ms P99, so they need a temporary fix ASAP.

hemant_infra: Initiating migration to a single-tenant host now. Will route their pool to node-iso-07 and keep both old and new for 30m. ETA ~6min.

ingest-bot: Routing update: `pool-rh-012` moved to node-iso-07 at 09:02:51 UTC. Metrics streaming to s3/logs/rh-012/iso-check.jsonl

chloe_support: Customer confirmed reduced tail latencies after migration: P99 down to 210ms within 4 minutes. They also stopped seeing 429s.

tess_sre: Good confirmation — this proves noisy neighbor interference. Action items: capture pre/post perf counters for the old node, add automated detection (heuristic: P99 jump + MIG co-tenants >1 => mark possible interference), and add a quick UI control to toggle isolation for dedicated customers.

sam_eng: For the runtime, let's also audit KV cache locking. If slices trigger cross-slice serialization, we should allow per-slice KV updates in parallel when possible. File follow-up to eng-runtime: RT-issue-1726.

hemant_infra: Added perf artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/rh-012/1792004567/ (nvprof, nvml logs, `dmesg`). Notable logs: `nvgpu: L2 evictions high`, and occasional `OOM kill attempt suppressed` messages from driver.

matt_customer: AtlasHealth asked about billing credits for the ~1.5 hours of degraded performance. Any support guidance?

chloe_support: Offer a goodwill credit for the incident window (09:00-10:30 UTC) and prioritize their migration to a reserved single-tenant node if they opt-in. I'll draft an incident note and credit amount.

tess_sre: I'm going to tag this as Sev-3 and open a postmortem template. Please add logs and the customer timeline. Also let's update runbooks with a quick isolation playbook: `isolate-tenant.sh` and `check-mig-contention.sh` commands to run immediately when alerts fire.

sam_eng: One more thing — suggest we add a metric to the console: 'co-tenants per node' + 'p99 jitter delta' so support can detect these patterns earlier. I'll PR to console-metrics.

chloe_support: Summary / next steps for support: 1) Credit window and customer outreach (Chloe) 2) Postmortem & runbook updates (Tess) 3) Runtime KV audit (Sam) 4) Autoscaler policy tweak to prefer cold-spare nodes for dedicated pools (Hemant).

matt_customer: Thanks all — customer is happy with the isolation and the temporary mitigation. Please keep me posted on permanent fixes.

chloe_support: Will do. Closing thread when postmortem and credit are confirmed. :white_check_mark:
